However, traditional methods for TOC detection require a high consumption of time and resources. To overcome these drawbacks, in this paper, a rapid and effective TOC detection method is developed based on near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and an improved convolutional neural network (CNN). Firstly, the spectrum of the water samples is collected using a portable near-infrared spectrometer. Then a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is integrated with one-dimensional CNN to effectively extract key characteristics of pollutants and achieve accurate quantitative analysis. The feature visualization results demonstrate the effectiveness of the feature extraction. And comparison experimental results shown that, the proposed method model has the greatest coefficient of determination and the smallest root mean square error compared with other models. Thus, the proposed method can accurately detect the total organic carbon in water and is suitable for practical applications.

articleTitle: Research on Navigation Light Sheets Cleaning Target Detection Technology Based on YOLO-v5s
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Carrying out the cleaning and maintenance of airport navigation light sheets is crucial for ensuring safe aircraft takeoff and landing, and the detection of navigation light sheets is the fundamental step in this process. In this study, we utilized the YOLO-v5s system to establish a target detection model for navigation lights and conducted experiments involving image annotation, parameter selection, model construction, model training, and prediction. The research findings demonstrate that the YOLO-v5s target detection model has reasonable parameter selection and achieves accurate training results. The recognition accuracy of the navigation light target detection model is 95.8%, with a mAP@0.5 value of 95% and a Recall value of 94%, indicating that the model's predictions meet the requirements for precision and real-time performance in practical applications. Moreover, the model exhibits high intelligent recognition accuracy in different conditions, such as normal and low light conditions, demonstrating excellent generalization ability and robustness, making it suitable for complex engineering scenarios in practice.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of KNN Classification Algorithm on Large-Scale Datasets: Real-Time Optimization Strategy Based on Balanced KD Tree and Multi-threaded Parallel Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm is a classical supervised learning method widely used in classification and regression problems. However, the KNN algorithm faces serious challenges when dealing with high-dimensional large-scale datasets, mainly in terms of high computational complexity, low search efficiency, and difficulty in real time. In this study, an optimization strategy based on balanced KD tree and multithreaded parallel computing is proposed to address this problem. Experimental results show that the optimized KNN algorithm significantly improves the search speed while maintaining classification accuracy, realizes real-time classification of large-scale datasets, and provides a powerful tool for pattern recognition, data mining, and other fields in the era of big data.

articleTitle: Design of an Industrial Workshop Equipment Maintenance System Based on HoloLens
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Following the modern information technology revolution, traditional manual operation and maintenance in the industrial field face challenges such as intricate and complex equipment, low technical proficiency of workers in maintenance, and increased intensity and costs of maintenance due to the addition of workshop equipment. To address these issues, this paper proposes an industrial workshop equipment maintenance system based on HoloLens. The system utilizes low-cost mature technologies to reduce deployment expenses and lower the entry barriers, thus simplifying the complexity of the maintenance system. Additionally, the system employs data reading and a graphical user interface to facilitate the understanding and use of front-line workers. Through this maintenance system, workers can efficiently carry out daily inspections and equipment maintenance tasks. In the event of unresolved issues, workers can use the system to communicate with experts remotely via video, enabling experts to provide real-time guidance for on-site problem-solving.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model Based on GAT and TAGCN for Node Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has been developing rapidly, especially the graph neural network plays an increasingly important role on more and more non-Euclidean data structures, such as social networks, recommender systems, molecular structures and other fields, and thus develops more rapidly. Convolutional operation has shown very good feature extraction effect on 2D data because of its translation without deformation, and its extension to graph convolutional networks on non-Euclidean data can also produce very good results. Now there are many very mature graph convolutional network algorithms, but although they can achieve good results on specific data structures, there are still some limitations. The hybrid model is able to make good use of its strengths and avoid its weaknesses. In this paper, we propose the AT-TAGCN model for node classification of graphs. Firstly, we construct the GAT model and TAGCN model respectively, and design their neural network layers, and then we combine the two, first use the neural network layer of GAT to process and then use the network layer of TAGCN to process, and then pass forward according to the corresponding order, and do the mean processing to get the final result, meanwhile, we use the dropout layer and the L2 regularization to alleviate the overfitting condition, so as to categorize the data of the graph Classification. In this paper, the CORA dataset is selected for the classification data. The results show that this method is more effective than the traditional methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Spatial Transformation and Attention Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Face super-resolution reconstruction is a critical task in various application domains. To fully leverage facial pose and texture information, we propose a novel algorithm for face super-resolution reconstruction that incorporates multi-scale spatial transformation and attention mechanisms. Firstly, the multi-scale spatial transformation is employed to learn the facial pose and perform affine transformations, enhancing the local information of the face image. Additionally, spatial attention is utilized to extract features in the image space, capturing global characteristics. Subsequently, a residual learning approach and a multi-path connected up-sampling module are employed to progressively increase the image resolution, reducing feature loss and training instability during the up-sampling process. Finally, a multi-scale convolution is utilized to reconstruct high-resolution facial images. The performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) as objective evaluation metrics. Experimental evaluations, conducted on the CelebA dataset at magnifications of 4x and 8x, demonstrate that our model achieves improved reconstruction of edge and texture information, as well as significant enhancements in the objective evaluation indicators of PSNR and SSIM.

articleTitle: Intelligent Driving Sensor Data Tampering Risk Detection Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the continuous development of intelligent driving technology, the reliability of sensor data is crucial to ensure driving safety and improve the performance of automatic driving. However, in the face of increasingly sophisticated and intelligent attack methods, the risk of tampering with sensor data is also increasing. Therefore, this study aims to develop an intelligent driving sensor data tampering risk detection method based on convolutional neural networks to effectively address this challenge. This paper firstly analyzes the potential threat of sensor data tampering to driving safety and system performance in intelligent driving system. Secondly, we propose a risk detection framework based on convolutional neural networks to identify and detect tampering of sensor data. The framework combines the advantages of convolutional neural networks to determine whether the data has been tampered with by learning the feature representation of sensor data. We designed a deep convolutional neural network model with multiple convolutional layers and pooled layers, and trained and validated it with a large amount of real driving data. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we constructed a dataset containing different types of attacks and compared it with other commonly used tamper detection methods.

articleTitle: KNCD: Knowledge-Enhanced Network for Cyberbullying Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In the past few years, the growth of online social networks has led to an increasingly serious problem of cyberbullying, making its detection a pressing issue. In this study, we propose the Knowledge Enhancement Network for Cyberbullying Detection (KNCD), an approach that utilizes the Large Language Model (LLM) to extract global information from the labeled data to enhance the knowledge of individual samples. Specifically, KNCD extracts essential information from representative samples with the LLM. After text encoding, the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) approach is applied to align this extracted knowledge with the samples. By combining the global knowledge with the samples, the semantic information of the samples is expanded. Experimental results on tweet data show that our KNCD model achieves promising performance in cyberbullying detection.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Approach to Bilingual Lexicon Induction with Comparable Corpora
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The steady growth of globalization leads to an increasing requirement for translations among different languages and an urgent need to keep pace with the challenge of cross-lingual international exchanges in multiple fields. Bilingual lexica are important language resources that provide valuable information for semantic equivalence of words across Languages, which has been a research hotspot. However, under resource-poor scenarios, it is difficult to find sufficient cross-lingual knowledge for model training, which requires the exploration of unsupervised learning methods. Unsupervised BLI aims at obtaining the bilingual translation dictionary from monolingual corpora of source and target languages without any cross-lingual knowledge, which can bring huge benefits to NLP tasks in resource-poor fields. Based on previous research, this thesis proposes a neural bilingual lexicon induction (NBLI) method with comparable corpora. This unsupervised method jointly learns word embeddings of source and target languages in the same vector space based on a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network, and then matches translation pairs through the Cross-domain Similarity Local Scaling (CSLS) retrieval to implement the induction task. It performs well in the general domain and improves the induction performance in the optoelectronic domain between English and Chinese, which breaks the limitation of the pure linear transformation model based on isomorphic assumption in resource-poor scenarios and solves the hubness problem in the bilingual vector space. Furthermore, it requires only comparable corpora in the model training process, and is applicable to various language pairs and specific fields.

articleTitle: Dam Face Crack Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Image analysis-based discrimination of dam face defects in hydropower stations is an efficient and accurate method, however, the dam crack images have problems such as complex background and uneven cracks and proportions, which lead to the poor detection effect of traditional algorithms. The paper proposes a dam face crack detection method based on the improved YOLOv5 model. A method is proposed to replace the CSP2_1 module with the BoT3 module based on self-attention mechanism in the backbone network to improve the model's ability to extract global features; and to add the lightweight hybrid attention mechanism HAM (Hybrid Attention Module) at the output of the backbone network to enhance the model's ability to capture important features to improve the model's convergence efficiency and accelerate the convergence speed. The results show that: The values of F1, score, Mean Intersection Over Union (MIoU) and Mean Pixel Accuracy (MPA), which are used to evaluate the accuracy of the model in the method, reach 73.98%, 66.73% and 73.81%, respectively, which are higher than those of the pre-improved The YOLOv5 detection effect was improved by 3.33%, 2.89% and 1.1%, respectively, and the method can provide technical support for the maintenance of the dam surface as well as the future risk assessment.

articleTitle: Design of Interactive Device for Pressure Evaluation Based on Expression Recognition and Heart Rate Variability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Under the COVID-19 pandemic, social and economic development has been slow, and more and more people are working longer hours. The pressure from work and life has put everyone in a tense and anxious environment, but only a few people understand and care about their own stress levels. With the development of heart rate variability measurement technology, the measurement method has become more convenient and efficient. However, there is no data visualization for the evaluation process, and users' stereotypes about stress evaluation are difficult to break, and the evaluation atmosphere is rather serious and boring. This design evaluates users' stress levels based on emotion recognition and heart rate variability analysis, and displays the evaluation process through data visualization and interactive devices to improve user experience and create a relaxed and interesting evaluation atmosphere.

articleTitle: Research on Substation Diagram Automatic Generation Based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the development of smart grids, intelligent image recognition technology has been applied to the automatic generation of power grid station wiring diagrams. The paper proposes a set of automatic mapping methods for power system station wiring diagrams based on artificial intelligence algorithms to improve the accuracy of station diagram recognition. Firstly, this algorithm introduces YOLOv5 to detect electrical elements and solve the problem of identifying electrical elements in the power grid station wiring diagram; Secondly, the algorithm in the paper introduces PP-OCR to detect electrical text, improving the accuracy of electrical text recognition in power grid station diagrams; Finally, based on the obtained bus information, identify the connection relationship to improve the accuracy of wiring identification. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method achieves good performance, with an accuracy rate of 95% for electrical element recognition and 93% for text recognition, meeting the requirements for automatic generation of factory station diagrams.

Author Keywords: Identification of power grid station wiring diagrams

articleTitle: Visual Analysis and Recognition of Virtual Reality Resolution Based on Pupil Response and Galvanic Skin Response
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The ability to efficiently assess the resolution of VR videos is critical for the implementation and advertising of VR products. Pupil responses and Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) are direct and objective mirrors of the emotional activity of humans. They are unaffected by subjective will and has excellent real-time performance, which can be used for VR quality assessment. However, there is little work to combine the two signals to evaluate VR resolution so far. Whether subjects' visual patterns alter with the VR resolution changes is also an interesting point that has not been studied yet. In this paper, a dataset containing subjects' pupil responses and GSR under different VR resolutions was built. Based on it, Area of Interest (AOI) was utilized to analyze subjects' visual patterns and found there were differences and similarities under varied VR video resolutions. To extract signal features at different VR resolutions more efficiently, a hybrid attention network was proposed. Experiment results demonstrated that the model can distinguish pupil responses and GSR signals under different VR video resolutions more efficiently, providing a feasibility verification for us to detect VR video resolutions using physiological signals.

articleTitle: Human-Centered HMI Design for Level 3 Automated Driving Takeover Process
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Most road safety accidents are caused by driver fatigue and distraction. Autonomous driving is recognised as enabling a safer road environment. In order to realise Sustainability Development Goal (SDG), the development of a more efficient HMI system to facilitate the takeover process is necessary. Level 3 automatic vehicles as a research subject, the article investigares the comprehensive human-machine interface (HMI) that promotes driver takeover effiency and safety under fatigue and distraction. This article employs a human-centered design (HCD) approach as its research methodology. The literature review investigates the factors influencing the efficiency of takeovers. Users requirements were uncovered and refined by questionnaires and in-person interviews. As a consequence of the HCD method research, the new HMI was designed as a multi-modes takeover alter system with two phases of cascading warnings. The interaction design for driver and dynamic information between seat, steering, pedal and windscreen. To further reduce the possibility of human error, the steering wheel and pedals also need periodical restrictions. The HMI design need be validated its efficiency in future investigations using driving simulators and on-road testing.

articleTitle: Research on Design of Visual Simulation Evaluation System Oriented to Ergonomics
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper addresses the need for a standardized Chinese human body model library in visual simulation evaluation tools for ergonomics analysis. The study investigates various evaluation methods such as Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA), NIOSH 1981, NIOSH 1991, Snook & Ciriello 1991, among others. Using open-source component packages such as QT, OGRE, and OPENCV, an ergonomics-oriented visual simulation evaluation system is designed. The system enables visualization of scene construction, human activity design, simulation, and human-mechanical ergonomics evaluation. Leveraging the Chinese human body standard model, a human-machine activity simulation case similar to DELMIA is developed. The effectiveness and feasibility of the system design are validated by comparing the analysis results of human-machine ergonomics evaluation.

articleTitle: Modeling Operational Profile for AI Systems: A Case Study on UAV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Operational profile (OP) and reliability testing is vital to ensure the reliability of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. This paper presents the AIOP (AI-oriented Operational Profile) method, which enhances reliability testing for AI systems, by incorporating environmental and data profiles to comprehensively represent their internal functioning and interaction with the external environment. Through the implementation of the AIOP framework and the introduction of feature-oriented profile modeling for environmental and data profiles, this study offers valuable insights for improving system reliability and reducing potential risks in the development and testing of AI systems across various domains. A case study on the UAV system, DroneResponse, demonstrates the effectiveness of the AIOP method.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning-Based Multi-Modal Entity Alignment and Feature Fusion Method for Electric Power Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper proposes a Contrastive Learning-Based Multi-Modal Entity Alignment and Feature Fusion Method (CMEAF) for addressing the challenge of poor entity alignment in Chinese electric power knowledge graph retrieval tasks. Firstly, we combine the ideas of multi-modal contrastive learning from CLIP and momentum contrastive learning from MoCo to design an improved contrastive loss function (MCCL). By introducing a more flexible negative sample selection strategy and incorporating momentum updates, the performance of contrastive learning is enhanced. Secondly, in the multi-modal feature fusion stage, we propose a Cross-Modal Attention Fusion (CMAF) method that leverages cross-modal attention mechanisms to fully exploit the interactive information between image and text features, achieving superior multi-modal feature fusion. Lastly, in the model pre-processing stage, we adopt the Mixup data augmentation idea and propose a Joint Data Augmentation approach based on image-text pairs (TMIXUP) to enhance downstream retrieval performance. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements of our proposed method in multi-modal entity alignment and feature fusion tasks. Compared to the baseline model WUKONG, CMEAF achieves a 2.5% increase in average recall rate on the MUGE dataset and a 4.1% improvement in MR performance on the Flickr30k-CN dataset. On the self-built POWER dataset, CMEAF also achieves excellent retrieval performance with an MR score of 93.7%. Furthermore, this paper conducts visual analysis to further showcase the advantages of multi-modal fusion. The proposed method effectively aligns Chinese cross-modal entities with high accuracy and practicality.

articleTitle: TMFER: Multimodal Fusion Emotion Recognition Algorithm Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: According to the problems of the existing emotion recognition algorithms, which are not rich in emotion information, weak in feature representation and not high in recognition accuracy, this paper proposes a multimodal fusion emotion recognition algorithm based on Transformer (TMFER), which fuses three modalities of text, speech and image information for emotion recognition. For the different characteristics of each modal information, Bert model pre-training processing, MFCC feature extraction and CNN feature extractor extraction methods are used to extract features for each modality respectively, to explore deeper features. To address the problem of unreasonable combination of multi-modal features, the Transformer Encode multi-headed attention mechanism is used to build a feature fusion module to extract and combine potential feature information in different modalities in parallel. The fused data are fed into the algorithm classification module for sentiment recognition classification, and a joint supervised loss function based on large margin learning is customized to solve the problem of unbalanced classification and feature confounding in the baseline model. Finally, based on the IEMOCAP and MELD multimodal datasets, the TMFER algorithm is experimentally compared with current algorithms in the field that are more effective in emotion recognition classification. The experimental results show that the TMFER algorithm outperforms other algorithms in all evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Enhanced Implicit Collaborative Knowledge Graph for Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Knowledge-aware Recommendation (KGR) with Graph Neural Network (GNN) aggregates information on the knowledge graph to capture high-order knowledge representations for the recommendation task, which becomes the mainstream approaches in the field of KGR. While these studies have achieved great success, we emphasize that strict supervision signals of training can have negative impacts on the model. Specifically, the supervision signals force the model to align constantly with sparse positive interaction data, which can result in the loss of valuable knowledge semantics. Moreover, it may also weaken model's ability to explore the potential interests for user. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose a new model named Enhanced Implicit Collaborative Knowledge Graph for Recommendation (EICKR), which uses a multi-task learning schema to extract user interests. This model calculates implicit relations among users, items, and entities to structure rich implicit features across different views. Subsequently, it leverages the knowledge graph and users' historical interaction data to generate an implicit collaborative knowledge graph, bridging the semantic difference between the knowledge graph and interaction data. Furthermore, a graph-enhanced completion task based on implicit relations is introduced to explore unobserved yet valuable interaction features among users, items, and entities, which can be complementary to the recommendation task. We conduct extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, which demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach and its components.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Task Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Recurrence Prediction by Knowledge Distillation with Loss-Balanced Weighting Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Recurrence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) generally leads to a poor prognosis, and a recurrence prediction method based on Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is valuable and meaningful for clinical treatment. However, a major challenge in effective prediction is the obvious difficulty of learning both global and local anatomical information from the tumor, due to irregular spatial representations in various MRI data. To address these issues, we construct a hard-parameter-sharing multi-task network for NPC recurrence prediction enhanced by Similarity-Preserving Knowledge Distillation (SPKD) with loss-balanced weighting strategy. In our method, the backbone generates global anatomical information and the auxiliary segmentation task extracts local anatomical information. Besides, through SPKD, the valuable hidden representations of single-task predictive network are distilled into the primary network and ease the negative transfer in the multi-task framework. Furthermore, we explore that the loss-balanced weighting strategy might not only reduce negative transfer but also constrain distillation of over-confidence knowledge, and the proper distilling layers positions in our framework encourage positive learning in specific knowledge-sharing tasks. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed multi-task learning (MTL) framework enhanced by similarity distillation knowledge distillation with loss-balanced weighting algorithm improves the overall performance.

articleTitle: Respiratory Disease Classification Model Based on Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The traditional methods for detecting respiratory system diseases have limitations such as invasiveness, high costs, and dosage restrictions. Therefore, it is of great significance to research and develop non-invasive, cost-effective, and convenient methods for lung audio classification. Due to the limited availability and imbalance of publicly available lung audio datasets, data augmentation techniques are used to balance the dataset and reduce the risk of overfitting. To comprehensively and accurately describe the characteristics of lung audio, time-frequency analysis techniques are employed to convert the audio into spectrograms, mel-spectrograms, and MFCC time-frequency representations as feature spectrograms, which are fused as the input to a neural network. A deep separable convolutional neural network with residual connections is proposed, and an attention mechanism is incorporated to enhance the network's focus on important features, aiming to achieve lung audio classification. The performance of the model is evaluated using the ICBHI-2017 dataset for lung audio recognition. In the six-class pathological audio classification task, the accuracy, sensitivity, precision, and F1 score reached 88.5%, 87.9%, 89.4%, and 88.3%, respectively. This approach demonstrates practical application value and promising prospects for lung audio recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Information Fusion Interface of Human-Computer Interaction based on Mixed Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that high-dimensional mixed reality interface brings low task performance and heavy cognitive load to users in cross-layer operation, we study the information fusion interface of human-computer interaction and propose two kinds of fusion interfaces. The experimental results show that the deep fusion interface performs better than the combined interface in cognitive difficulty, cognitive load, operational efficiency and subjective evaluation. The research conclusion can guide the design of human-computer interaction interface in mixed reality.

articleTitle: Optimization of Pose Recognition Algorithms in Smart Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the surge in popularity of smart wearable devices, the necessity for pose recognition has become paramount, especially in fields like motion analysis, health monitoring, and virtual reality. Yet, achieving efficient and precise pose recognition on devices with limited resources poses significant hurdles. Addressing this, we introduce an innovative optimization method for pose recognition algorithms, harnessing the power of the C++ compiler. Our approach uniquely integrates traditional machine learning paradigms with model simplification techniques. Furthermore, by exploiting C++ functionalities such as inline assembly, template metaprogramming, and compile-time optimization, we craft an optimization tailored explicitly for wearable hardware. Evaluations conducted on various devices testify to our method's superiority, marking a 10% surge in accuracy, 30% boost in efficiency, and a 15% dip in energy consumption relative to contemporary methods. Apart from achieving stellar accuracy and real-time performance, our method distinguishes itself in resource efficiency and scalability. This article offers an in-depth exploration of our design philosophies, optimization tactics, experimentation methodologies, and seminal discoveries, signposting the future trajectory of pose recognition in smart wearables and highlighting its commercial potential.

articleTitle: Exploratory Design Research on Interaction System for L3 Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper starts from the shortcomings of the current domestic L3 autonomous driving interactive system design combined with the safety, responsibility, and task challenges it faces, and tries to clarify the main differences between L3 and L2(and below) automatic driving systems, and proposes an interaction model for L3 automatic driving vehicles. Based on the model and referring to the requirements of the autonomous driving regulations on the interaction level, the interactive system design is carried out. The research focusing on safety, responsibility and tasks proposes a TSE design method (driving training, driving safety and performance evaluation) to conduct closed-loop design of L3 autonomous vehicle interaction. The research combines norms and standards such as ethical guidelines, regulations, and exposure draft to summarize the requirements for human-computer interaction. It provides a certain guiding significance for the research and design practice of the current human-computer interaction direction of autonomous driving.
